title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Biology and Living Processes
text:
Biology and Living Processes

Key terms: biology, living processes

Biology is the science of life forms and living processes. It studies the diversity of living organisms and their interactions with the environment. The field of biology has evolved over time, from early observations of living organisms to the development of systematic and monumental descriptions of life forms.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Diversity in the Living World
text:
Diversity in the Living World

Key terms: diversity, living world

The living world is characterized by an amazing diversity of living organisms. From plants and animals to microorganisms, the range of living types is vast and complex. This diversity is a result of millions of years of evolution and adaptation to different environments.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Classification and Nomenclature
text:
Classification and Nomenclature

Key terms: classification, nomenclature

Classification is the process of grouping living organisms into categories based on their characteristics. Nomenclature is the system of naming living organisms using a two-word format, with the genus and species names. This system helps to standardize the naming of living organisms and facilitates communication among biologists.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Taxonomic Categories
text:
Taxonomic Categories

Key terms: taxonomic categories, kingdom, phylum

Taxonomic categories include kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, and species. Each category represents a rank or level of classification, with the species being the lowest category. Taxonomic categories help to group living organisms based on their characteristics and evolutionary relationships.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Taxonomic Categories in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Species and Genus
text:
Species and Genus

Key terms: species, genus

A species is a group of individual organisms with fundamental similarities. A genus is a group of related species that share more characters in common. Species and genus are the basic units of classification and are used to group living organisms based on their characteristics and evolutionary relationships.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Species and Genus in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Family and Order
text:
Family and Order

Key terms: family, order

A family is a group of related genera that share still fewer similarities. An order is a group of families that exhibit a few similar characters. Families and orders are higher categories of classification that group living organisms based on their characteristics and evolutionary relationships.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Family and Order in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Systematics and Taxonomy
text:
Systematics and Taxonomy

Key terms: systematics, taxonomy

Systematics is the branch of study that deals with the relationships among living organisms. Taxonomy is the process of classifying living organisms based on their characteristics and evolutionary relationships. Systematics and taxonomy are closely related fields that help to understand the diversity of living organisms and their interactions with the environment.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Systematics and Taxonomy in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Taxonomic Hierarchy
text:
Taxonomic Hierarchy

Key terms: taxonomy, classification, hierarchy

The taxonomic hierarchy is a system used to classify living organisms. It consists of several categories, including species, genus, family, order, class, phylum, and kingdom. Each category is more general than the previous one, with kingdom being the most general. This hierarchy helps us understand the relationships between different organisms.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Taxonomic Hierarchy in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Kingdom Classification
text:
Kingdom Classification

Key terms: kingdom, animalia, plantae

The kingdom is the highest category in the taxonomic hierarchy. There are two main kingdoms: Animalia and Plantae. Animalia includes all animals, while Plantae includes all plants. These kingdoms are based on the characteristics of the organisms, such as the presence of a notochord and dorsal hollow neural system in animals.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Kingdom Classification in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Phylum and Division
text:
Phylum and Division

Key terms: phylum, division, chordata

Phylum is a category that includes classes with similar characteristics. In animals, phylum is used, while in plants, division is used. For example, the phylum Chordata includes animals with a notochord and dorsal hollow neural system, while the division Angiospermae includes plants with flowers.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Phylum and Division in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Class and Order
text:
Class and Order

Key terms: class, order, mammalia

Class is a category that includes related orders. Order is a category that includes related families. For example, the class Mammalia includes orders such as Primata and Carnivora, while the order Carnivora includes families such as Felidae and Canidae.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Class and Order in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Family and Genus
text:
Family and Genus

Key terms: family, genus, felidae

Family is a category that includes related genera. Genus is a category that includes related species. For example, the family Felidae includes genera such as Panthera and Felis, while the genus Panthera includes species such as lions and tigers.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Family and Genus in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Biological Classification
text:
Biological Classification

Key terms: Classification, Kingdoms

Biological classification is the process of grouping living organisms based on their characteristics and evolutionary relationships. It helps us understand the diversity of life on Earth and how different organisms are related to each other. The classification system has undergone several changes over time, with different scientists proposing different systems. The most widely used system is the Five Kingdom Classification, which groups organisms into Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, and Animalia.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Biological Classification in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Kingdom Monera
text:
Kingdom Monera

Key terms: Bacteria, Monera

Kingdom Monera consists of bacteria, which are single-celled microorganisms that lack a true nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles. They are found almost everywhere and can survive in extreme conditions. Bacteria can be autotrophic or heterotrophic, and they play a crucial role in decomposing organic matter and recycling nutrients. They can also cause diseases in humans, animals, and plants.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Kingdom Monera in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Kingdom Protista
text:
Kingdom Protista

Key terms: Protista, Eukaryotes

Kingdom Protista consists of single-celled eukaryotes that do not fit into any other kingdom. They are primarily aquatic and include organisms such as protozoans, algae, and slime moulds. Protists are diverse and can be photosynthetic or heterotrophic, and they play an important role in the ecosystem as producers and decomposers.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Kingdom Protista in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Kingdom Fungi
text:
Kingdom Fungi

Key terms: Fungi, Heterotrophs

Kingdom Fungi consists of heterotrophic organisms that obtain their nutrients by decomposing organic matter or by forming symbiotic relationships with other organisms. Fungi include mushrooms, moulds, and yeasts, and they play a crucial role in decomposing organic matter and recycling nutrients. Some fungi can also cause diseases in plants and animals.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Kingdom Fungi in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Five Kingdom Classification
text:
Five Kingdom Classification

Key terms: Five Kingdoms, Classification

The Five Kingdom Classification is a system of classification that groups organisms into five kingdoms: Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, and Animalia. This system is based on the characteristics of the organisms, such as cell structure, body organization, mode of nutrition, and evolutionary relationships. The Five Kingdom Classification is widely used and provides a framework for understanding the diversity of life on Earth.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Five Kingdom Classification in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Fungi: Unique Kingdom
text:
Fungi: Unique Kingdom

Key terms: heterotrophic, decomposers, parasites, symbionts

Fungi are heterotrophic organisms with diverse morphology and habitats. They include mushrooms, yeasts, and molds. Some are decomposers, while others are parasites or symbionts. They prefer warm, humid places and are found in air, water, soil, and on plants and animals.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Fungal Structure
text:
Fungal Structure

Key terms: mycelium, hyphae, coenocytic, septate

Fungi have filamentous bodies called mycelium, composed of long, slender threads called hyphae. Hyphae can be coenocytic (without septae) or septate (with cross walls). Fungal cell walls are made of chitin and polysaccharides.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Fungal Structure in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Fungal Nutrition
text:
Fungal Nutrition

Key terms: saprophytes, parasites, symbionts

Most fungi are saprophytes, absorbing soluble organic matter from dead substrates. Some are parasites, depending on living plants or animals. A few live as symbionts with algae or plant roots.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Fungal Nutrition in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Fungal Reproduction
text:
Fungal Reproduction

Key terms: vegetative reproduction, asexual reproduction, sexual reproduction, meiosis

Fungi reproduce vegetatively by fragmentation, fission, or budding. Asexual reproduction is by spores like conidia or zoospores, while sexual reproduction involves fusion of protoplasm and nuclei, followed by meiosis.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Fungal Reproduction in Grade 11 Biology.

Biological Classification

Organisms are classified based on cell structure, body organization, mode of nutrition, reproduction, and phylogenetic relationships. The five-kingdom classification includes Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, and Animalia.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Kingdom Plantae
text:
Kingdom Plantae

Key terms: eukaryotic, chlorophyll-containing, cell wall, alternation of generations

Plants are eukaryotic, chlorophyll-containing organisms. They have a cell wall made of cellulose and exhibit alternation of generations in their life cycle.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Kingdom Animalia
text:
Kingdom Animalia

Key terms: heterotrophic, multicellular, no cell walls, sexual reproduction

Animals are heterotrophic, multicellular organisms without cell walls. They depend on plants for food, digest internally, and reproduce sexually by copulation and embryological development.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Kingdom Animalia in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Viruses, Viroids, Prions, and Lichens
text:
Viruses, Viroids, Prions, and Lichens

Key terms: viruses, viroids, prions, lichens, symbiosis

Viruses are non-cellular, obligate parasites with protein coats and genetic material (RNA or DNA). Viroids are smaller, free RNA without a protein coat. Prions are infectious proteins causing neurological diseases. Lichens are symbiotic associations between algae and fungi.

Algae are simple, aquatic, chlorophyll-bearing organisms with diverse forms and reproduction methods, including asexual (zoospores) and sexual (isogamous, anisogamous, oogamous).

Bryophytes have a thallus-like plant body with rhizoids, lack true roots, stems, or leaves, and reproduce sexually via antherozoids and archegonia, producing a sporophyte that is dependent on the gametophyte.

Pteridophytes: Plant Body and Vascular Tissues

Key terms: vascular tissues, xylem, phloem, sporophyte, dominant phase

Pteridophytes are the first terrestrial plants with vascular tissues (xylem and phloem), possessing true roots, stems, and leaves, with the sporophyte being the dominant phase.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Pteridophyte Life Cycle
text:
Pteridophyte Life Cycle

Key terms: sporophyte, gametophyte, spores, fertilization, zygote

Pteridophytes have a dominant sporophyte phase with true roots, stems, and leaves. They produce spores that germinate into small, multicellular, photosynthetic gametophytes. These require cool, damp places to grow and bear male (antheridia) and female (archegonia) sex organs. Fertilization occurs in water, resulting in a zygote that develops into a sporophyte.

metadata.subject: Biology

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Heterosporous Pteridophytes
text:
Heterosporous Pteridophytes

Key terms: heterosporous, microspores, megaspores, gametophytes, embryo

Some pteridophytes, like Selaginella and Salvinia, produce two types of spores: microspores and megaspores. These give rise to male and female gametophytes, respectively. The female gametophytes are retained on the parent sporophyte, and the zygote develops into an embryo within them.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Gymnosperm Reproduction
text:
Gymnosperm Reproduction

Key terms: microspores, megaspores, pollen grains, female gametophytes, fertilization, seeds

Gymnosperms produce microspores and megaspores within microsporangia and megasporangia on sporophylls. The microspores develop into pollen grains, and the megaspores into female gametophytes. Fertilization occurs when the pollen tube reaches the archegonia in the ovules, resulting in seed formation.

Angiosperms are divided into two classes: dicotyledons and monocotyledons. They range in size from tiny aquatic plants to tall trees and provide various commercially important products.

Bryophytes have a more differentiated plant body than algae, with root-like, leaf-like, and stem-like structures. The main plant body is a gamete-producing gametophyte that bears male (antheridia) and female (archegonia) sex organs.

Unlike gymnosperms, angiosperms have specialised structures called flowers for pollen and ovule development. After fertilization, the ovules are enclosed in fruits, and the seeds are not naked.

Regions of the Root

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Stem and Its Functions
text:
Stem and Its Functions

Key terms: stem, axis, branches, leaves, flowers, fruits, conducting, support, protection

The stem is the ascending part of the axis bearing branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits. Its main functions are spreading out branches, conducting water, minerals, and photosynthates, and providing support and protection.

text:
Leaf Structure and Function

Key terms: leaf, leaf base, petiole, lamina, photosynthesis, vegetative organ

A leaf is a lateral, flattened structure borne on the stem. It consists of a leaf base, petiole, and lamina. The main function of a leaf is photosynthesis, and it is the most important vegetative organ for this purpose.

text:
Venation in Leaves

Venation refers to the arrangement of veins and veinlets in the lamina of a leaf. It can be reticulate (network-like) or parallel, depending on the type of plant.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Venation in Leaves in Grade 11 Biology.

text:
Corolla Shapes and Aestivation

Key terms: corolla, aestivation, valvate, twisted, imbricate, vexillary

Corolla, the petals of a flower, can be tubular, bell-shaped, funnel-shaped, or wheel-shaped. title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Stamen Structure and Types
text:
Stamen Structure and Types

A stamen consists of a filament and an anther, where pollen grains are produced. Stamens can be free, united with other members like petals (epipetalous), or among themselves (monoadelphous, diadelphous, polyadelphous).

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Stamen Structure and Types in Grade 11 Biology.

Fruit and Seed Development

Floral Diagram and Formula

A floral diagram represents the arrangement of floral parts, while a floral formula uses symbols to describe the number and type of each part in a flower.

Epidermal Tissue System

The outermost layer of a plant, composed of epidermal cells, stomata, and appendages like trichomes and hairs. It protects the plant, regulates gas exchange, and prevents water loss.

The main bulk of the plant, consisting of simple tissues like parenchyma, collenchyma, and sclerenchyma. It performs various functions such as storage, support, and absorption.

The conducting tissue system, composed of xylem and phloem. It transports water, minerals, and food materials throughout the plant.

A stem with a sclerenchymatous hypodermis, scattered vascular bundles, and a large, conspicuous parenchymatous ground tissue. It has no secondary growth.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Cytokinins
text:
Cytokinins

Key terms: cytokinins, kinetin, zeatin

Cytokinins are PGRs that promote cell division, nutrient mobilisation, and delay leaf senescence. They are produced in regions where rapid cell division occurs.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Cytokinins in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Ethylene
text:
Ethylene

Key terms: ethylene, ethephon

Ethylene is a gaseous PGR that promotes ripening, abscission, and root growth. It is produced in large amounts by tissues undergoing senescence and ripening fruits.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Ethylene in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Abscisic Acid (ABA)
text:
Abscisic Acid (ABA)

Key terms: ABA, abscisic acid

ABA is a PGR that acts as a general plant growth inhibitor and an inhibitor of plant metabolism. It plays a role in seed development, maturation, and dormancy.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Abscisic Acid (ABA) in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Plant Growth and Development Control
text:
Plant Growth and Development Control

Key terms: intrinsic factors, extrinsic factors, PGRs

Plant growth and development are controlled by both intrinsic and extrinsic factors. Intrinsic factors include PGRs, while extrinsic factors include light, temperature, nutrition, etc.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Plant Growth and Development Control in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Plant Growth Phases
text:
Plant Growth Phases

Key terms: lag phase, log phase, senescent phase

Plant growth can be divided into three phases: lag, log, and senescent. Growth may not be sustained at a high rate throughout the life of a cell, tissue, organ, or organism.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Plant Growth Phases in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Respiratory Organs
text:
Respiratory Organs

Key terms: respiratory organs, lungs, alveoli

Different animals have various respiratory organs like gills, lungs, or skin for gas exchange, depending on their habitat and organization. Humans have a complex respiratory system with nostrils, nasal chamber, pharynx, larynx, trachea, bronchi, bronchioles, and alveoli in the lungs.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Respiratory Organs in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Mechanism of Breathing
text:
Mechanism of Breathing

Key terms: inspiration, expiration, diaphragm, intercostal muscles

Breathing involves two stages: inspiration (drawing in air) and expiration (releasing air). These are achieved by changing the pressure between the lungs and atmosphere using the diaphragm and intercostal muscles.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Mechanism of Breathing in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Respiratory Volumes and Capacities
text:
Respiratory Volumes and Capacities

Key terms: tidal volume, respiratory capacity, vital capacity

Respiratory volumes include tidal volume (air moved during normal breathing), inspiratory reserve volume, expiratory reserve volume, and residual volume. Pulmonary capacities are derived from these volumes, such as inspiratory capacity, expiratory capacity, functional residual capacity, vital capacity, and total lung capacity.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Respiratory Volumes and Capacities in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Exchange of Gases
text:
Exchange of Gases

Key terms: diffusion, partial pressure, solubility

Gases (O2 and CO2) diffuse between the alveoli and blood, and between blood and tissues, based on pressure gradients. The solubility of CO2 and the thickness of diffusion membranes also affect gas exchange.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Exchange of Gases in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Transport of Oxygen
text:
Transport of Oxygen

Key terms: hemoglobin, oxyhemoglobin, oxygen dissociation curve

Oxygen is transported in the blood by red blood cells (RBCs) containing hemoglobin, which can bind with O2. The oxygen-hemoglobin dissociation curve shows the relationship between the partial pressure of O2 and the percentage of hemoglobin saturated with O2.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Transport of Oxygen in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Oxygen Dissociation Curve
text:
Oxygen Dissociation Curve

Key terms: sigmoid curve, haemoglobin, oxygen binding

A sigmoid curve showing the percentage of haemoglobin saturated with oxygen at different partial pressures of oxygen. It helps study factors affecting oxygen binding to haemoglobin.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Oxygen Dissociation Curve in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Oxygen Transport by Haemoglobin
text:
Oxygen Transport by Haemoglobin

Key terms: haemoglobin, oxygen binding, pCO2, H+ concentration

Haemoglobin in red blood cells carries oxygen from the lungs to the tissues. The binding and release of oxygen are influenced by factors like pCO2, H+ concentration, and temperature.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Oxygen Transport by Haemoglobin in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Carbon Dioxide Transport
text:
Carbon Dioxide Transport

Key terms: carbon dioxide, haemoglobin, bicarbonate, carbonic anhydrase

Carbon dioxide is carried by haemoglobin as carbamino-haemoglobin (about 20-25%) and by red blood cells as bicarbonate (HCO3-) with the help of carbonic anhydrase.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Carbon Dioxide Transport in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Respiratory Rhythm Regulation
text:
Respiratory Rhythm Regulation

Key terms: respiratory rhythm, medulla, pons, chemosensitive area

The respiratory rhythm is maintained by a center in the medulla region of the brain, which can be modulated by a center in the pons region and a chemosensitive area sensitive to CO2 and H+ ions.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Respiratory Rhythm Regulation in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Asthma and Emphysema
text:
Asthma and Emphysema

Key terms: asthma, emphysema, bronchi, alveolar walls

Asthma is a breathing difficulty causing wheezing due to bronchi inflammation, while emphysema is a chronic disorder damaging alveolar walls and decreasing respiratory surface, often caused by cigarette smoking.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Asthma and Emphysema in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Gaseous Exchange in Respiration
text:
Gaseous Exchange in Respiration

Key terms: gaseous exchange, diffusion, partial pressure

Gases like oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged between the atmosphere, alveoli, blood, and tissues through diffusion, driven by partial pressure gradients.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Gaseous Exchange in Respiration in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Respiratory Volumes
text:
Respiratory Volumes

Key terms: respiratory volumes, tidal volume, inspiratory reserve volume, spirometer

Respiratory volumes include tidal volume, inspiratory reserve volume, expiratory reserve volume, inspiratory capacity, expiratory capacity, and vital capacity, which can be measured using a spirometer.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Respiratory Volumes in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Occupational Respiratory Disorders
text:
Occupational Respiratory Disorders

Key terms: occupational respiratory disorders, dust exposure, lung damage, protective masks

Certain industries with high dust exposure can lead to lung inflammation, fibrosis, and serious damage if workers do not wear protective masks.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Occupational Respiratory Disorders in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Blood Composition
text:
Blood Composition

Key terms: plasma, formed elements, RBCs, WBCs, platelets

Blood is a special connective tissue consisting of plasma (55%) and formed elements (45%). Plasma is mostly water (90-92%) with proteins (6-8%), while formed elements include red blood cells (RBCs), white blood cells (WBCs), and platelets.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Blood Composition in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Plasma Components
text:
Plasma Components

Key terms: fibrinogen, globulins, albumins, clotting factors

Plasma contains water, proteins (fibrinogen, globulins, albumins), minerals (Na+, Ca++, Mg++, HCO3-, Cl-), and substances in transit like glucose, amino acids, and lipids. It also has clotting factors in an inactive form.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Plasma Components in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Red Blood Cells (RBCs)
text:
Red Blood Cells (RBCs)

Key terms: hemoglobin, lifespan, biconcave

RBCs are the most abundant cells in blood, averaging 5 million to 5.5 million per mm3. They are biconcave in shape, lack a nucleus, and contain hemoglobin for oxygen transport. Their average lifespan is 120 days.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Red Blood Cells (RBCs) in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | White Blood Cells (WBCs)
text:
White Blood Cells (WBCs)

Key terms: granulocytes, agranulocytes, neutrophils, lymphocytes

WBCs, or leucocytes, are nucleated and fewer in number than RBCs, averaging 6000-8000 per mm3. They are involved in immune responses and include granulocytes (neutrophils, eosinophils, basophils) and agranulocytes (lymphocytes, monocytes).

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to White Blood Cells (WBCs) in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Blood Groups (ABO)
text:
Blood Groups (ABO)

Key terms: antigens, antibodies, universal donor, universal recipient

Blood is grouped into A, B, AB, and O based on the presence or absence of A and B antigens on RBCs and corresponding antibodies in plasma. Group 'O' can donate to any group, and group 'AB' can receive from any group.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Blood Groups (ABO) in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Rh Blood Group
text:
Rh Blood Group

Key terms: Rh antigen, Rh incompatibility, erythroblastosis foetalis

Rh grouping is based on the presence (Rh+) or absence (Rh-) of the Rh antigen on RBCs. Rh incompatibility between mother and fetus can cause severe problems, including erythroblastosis foetalis.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Rh Blood Group in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Blood Coagulation
text:
Blood Coagulation

Key terms: fibrinogens, thrombin, prothrombin, cascade process

Blood coagulation or clotting is a response to injury, preventing excessive blood loss. It involves the conversion of inactive fibrinogens to fibrin by thrombin, which is formed from prothrombin in a cascade process involving various factors.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Blood Coagulation in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Lymph (Tissue Fluid)
text:
Lymph (Tissue Fluid)

Key terms: lymphocytes, lymphatic system, nutrients, hormones

Lymph is a colourless fluid containing lymphocytes, responsible for immune responses. It is collected by the lymphatic system and drains into major veins. Lymph carries nutrients, hormones, and absorbed fats.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Lymph (Tissue Fluid) in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Cardiac Pacemaker
text:
Cardiac Pacemaker

Key terms: Sino-atrial node, Pacemaker, Heart rate

The sino-atrial node (SAN) generates electrical signals that cause the heart to beat. It's the heart's natural pacemaker, setting the pace for heart contractions at a rate of 70-75 beats per minute.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Cardiac Pacemaker in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Cardiac Cycle
text:
Cardiac Cycle

Key terms: Systole, Diastole, Cardiac cycle

The cardiac cycle is the sequence of events that occurs during one heartbeat. It consists of systole (contraction) and diastole (relaxation) of both atria and ventricles, lasting about 0.8 seconds.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Cardiac Cycle in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Electrocardiogram (ECG)
text:
Electrocardiogram (ECG)

Key terms: ECG, Electrical activity, Heart rhythm

An ECG is a graphical representation of the electrical activity of the heart during a cardiac cycle. It shows the heart's rhythm and can help diagnose heart problems.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Electrocardiogram (ECG) in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Pulmonary Circulation
text:
Pulmonary Circulation

Key terms: Pulmonary circulation, Pulmonary arteries, Pulmonary veins

Pulmonary circulation is the pathway of blood flow through the lungs. Deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle flows into the pulmonary arteries, is oxygenated in the lungs, and then returns to the left atrium via the pulmonary veins.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Pulmonary Circulation in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Systemic Circulation
text:
Systemic Circulation

Key terms: Systemic circulation, Aorta, Vena cava

Systemic circulation is the pathway of blood flow through the body. Oxygenated blood from the left ventricle flows into the aorta, is distributed to all body tissues, and then returns to the right atrium via the vena cava.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Systemic Circulation in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Heart Sounds
text:
Heart Sounds

Key terms: Heart sounds, Atrioventricular valves, Semilunar valves

Heart sounds are the sounds produced by the heart's valves closing during the cardiac cycle. The first heart sound (lub) is associated with the closure of the atrioventricular valves, and the second heart sound (dub) is associated with the closure of the semilunar valves.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Heart Sounds in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Hypertension
text:
Hypertension

Key terms: Hypertension, Blood pressure, Heart diseases

Hypertension is high blood pressure, typically defined as a systolic blood pressure greater than 140 mmHg or a diastolic blood pressure greater than 90 mmHg. It can lead to heart diseases and affect vital organs like the brain and kidneys.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Hypertension in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Coronary Artery Disease (CAD)
text:
Coronary Artery Disease (CAD)

Key terms: CAD, Atherosclerosis, Heart attacks

CAD, also known as atherosclerosis, is a disease in which the arteries that supply blood to the heart muscle become hardened and narrowed due to the buildup of calcium, fat, cholesterol, and fibrous tissues. This can lead to heart attacks.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Ammonotelism
text:
Ammonotelism

Key terms: ammonia, aquatic animals, excrete

Ammonotelism is the process of excreting ammonia as the primary nitrogenous waste. Many aquatic animals, like bony fishes and aquatic amphibians, use this method.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Ammonotelism in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Ureotelism
text:
Ureotelism

Key terms: urea, terrestrial animals, excrete

Ureotelism is the process of excreting urea as the primary nitrogenous waste. Many terrestrial animals, like mammals and terrestrial amphibians, use this method to conserve water.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Ureotelism in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Uricotelism
text:
Uricotelism

Key terms: uric acid, reptiles, birds, excrete

Uricotelism is the process of excreting uric acid as the primary nitrogenous waste. Reptiles, birds, and some insects use this method to minimize water loss.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Uricotelism in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR)
text:
Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR)

Key terms: GFR, kidney function, blood filtration

GFR is the amount of blood filtered by the kidneys per minute. It's an important indicator of kidney function.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR) in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Reabsorption
text:
Reabsorption

Key terms: reabsorption, filtrate, kidneys

Reabsorption is the process by which the kidneys reabsorb useful substances, like water and electrolytes, from the filtrate back into the blood.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Reabsorption in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Tubular Secretion
text:
Tubular Secretion

Key terms: tubular secretion, kidneys, acid-base balance

Tubular secretion is the process by which the kidneys secrete substances, like hydrogen ions and potassium, into the filtrate to maintain the body's acid-base balance.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Tubular Secretion in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Counter Current Mechanism
text:
Counter Current Mechanism

Key terms: counter current mechanism, Henle's loop, vasa recta, urine concentration

This mechanism, involving Henle's loop and vasa recta, helps the kidneys to produce concentrated urine by creating an osmotic gradient in the medullary interstitium.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Counter Current Mechanism in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Micturition
text:
Micturition

Key terms: micturition, urination, bladder, urethra

Micturition is the voluntary process of urination, involving the storage of urine in the bladder and its expulsion through the urethra.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to create concepts related to Micturition in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Urine Formation Process
text:
Urine Formation Process

Key terms: filtration, reabsorption, secretion

Urine formation involves three main processes: filtration, reabsorption, and secretion. Filtration is performed by the glomerulus, reabsorption occurs through different parts of the nephrons, and secretion helps maintain ionic balance and pH.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Urine Formation Process in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Nephron Structure
text:
Nephron Structure

Key terms: nephron, glomerulus, renal tubule

Nephron is the functional unit of the kidney, consisting of a glomerulus and a renal tubule. The renal tubule has three parts: proximal convoluted tubule, Henle's loop, and distal convoluted tubule.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Nephron Structure in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Micturition Process
text:
Micturition Process

Key terms: micturition, bladder, urethral sphincter

Micturition is the process of releasing urine from the bladder, initiated by a voluntary signal from the central nervous system. It involves the contraction of smooth muscles of the bladder and relaxation of the urethral sphincter.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Micturition Process in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Counter Current Mechanism
text:
Counter Current Mechanism

Key terms: counter current mechanism, Henle's loop, vasa recta

This mechanism operates between the two limbs of the loop of Henle and those of vasa recta, helping to concentrate the filtrate as it moves down the descending limb but diluting it by the ascending limb.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Counter Current Mechanism in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Role of Other Organs in Excretion
text:
Role of Other Organs in Excretion

Key terms: lungs, liver, skin, excretion

Besides the kidneys, lungs, liver, and skin also help in the elimination of excretory wastes. Lungs remove CO2 and water, the liver secretes bile, and the skin eliminates certain substances through sweat and sebum.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.topic: Role of Other Organs in Excretion
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Role of Other Organs in Excretion in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR)
text:
Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR)

Key terms: GFR, glomerulus, kidney function

GFR is the volume of blood plasma filtered by the glomerulus per minute. It's an important indicator of kidney function, with a normal value being around 120 ml/min.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR) in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Autoregulatory Mechanism of GFR
text:
Autoregulatory Mechanism of GFR

Key terms: GFR, juxtaglomerular apparatus, autoregulation

The juxtaglomerular apparatus (JGA) plays a significant role in regulating GFR by adjusting the diameter of the afferent and efferent arterioles based on blood pressure and other factors.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Autoregulatory Mechanism of GFR in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Disorders of the Excretory System
text:
Disorders of the Excretory System

Key terms: uremia, hemodialysis, kidney transplantation

Malfunctioning of the kidneys can lead to conditions like uremia, which is harmful and may lead to kidney failure. Treatments include hemodialysis and kidney transplantation.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Disorders of the Excretory System in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Types of Movement
text:
Types of Movement

Key terms: amoeboid, ciliary, muscular

Cells exhibit three main types: amoeboid (like Amoeba), ciliary (e.g., in trachea), and muscular (e.g., limbs).

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Types of Movement in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Locomotion vs Movement
text:
Locomotion vs Movement

Key terms: locomotion, movement

All locomotion is movement, but not all movement is locomotion. Locomotion involves change of place.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Locomotion vs Movement in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Purpose of Locomotion
text:
Purpose of Locomotion

Key terms: food, shelter, mate, escape

Animals locomote for food, shelter, mate, breeding grounds, favorable climate, or to escape enemies.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Purpose of Locomotion in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Muscle Types
text:
Muscle Types

Key terms: skeletal, visceral, cardiac

Three types of muscles: skeletal (voluntary, striated), visceral (involuntary, smooth), and cardiac (involuntary, striated).

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Muscle Types in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Muscle Structure
text:
Muscle Structure

Key terms: myofilaments, sarcomeres, striations

Muscle fibers contain myofilaments (actin and myosin) arranged in sarcomeres, causing striations.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Muscle Structure in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Muscle Contraction
text:
Muscle Contraction

Key terms: sliding filament, actin, myosin

Sliding filament theory: actin and myosin filaments slide over each other, causing muscle shortening.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Muscle Contraction in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Skeletal System Components
text:
Skeletal System Components

Key terms: axial, appendicular, skull, vertebrae

Axial skeleton (skull, vertebral column, sternum, ribs) and appendicular skeleton (limbs).

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Skeletal System Components in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Rib Types
text:
Rib Types

Key terms: true ribs, vertebrochondral ribs, floating ribs

True ribs (1-7), vertebrochondral ribs (8-10), and floating ribs (11-12).

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Rib Types in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Ribs and Rib Cage
text:
Ribs and Rib Cage

Key terms: ribs, thoracic vertebrae, sternum, floating ribs

Ribs are bones that protect the lungs and heart. They attach dorsally to the thoracic vertebrae and ventrally to the sternum. The 11th and 12th pairs are called floating ribs as they are not connected ventrally.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Ribs and Rib Cage in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Vertebrochondral Ribs
text:
Vertebrochondral Ribs

Key terms: vertebrochondral ribs, hyaline cartilage, sternum

The 8th, 9th, and 10th pairs of ribs do not articulate directly with the sternum. Instead, they join the seventh rib with the help of hyaline cartilage, making them false or vertebrochondral ribs.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Vertebrochondral Ribs in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Bones of the Limbs
text:
Bones of the Limbs

Key terms: humerus, radius, ulna, carpals, metacarpals, phalanges, femur, tibia, fibula, tarsals, metatarsals

Each limb consists of 30 bones: humerus, radius, ulna, carpals, metacarpals, phalanges for the fore limb, and femur, tibia, fibula, tarsals, metatarsals, phalanges for the hind limb.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Bones of the Limbs in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Pectoral and Pelvic Girdles
text:
Pectoral and Pelvic Girdles

Key terms: pectoral girdle, clavicle, scapula, pelvic girdle, coxal bones, ilium, ischium, pubis

The pectoral girdle consists of the clavicle and scapula, while the pelvic girdle is made up of two coxal bones, each formed by the fusion of the ilium, ischium, and pubis.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Pectoral and Pelvic Girdles in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Joints
text:
Joints

Key terms: joints, fibrous joints, cartilaginous joints, synovial joints

Joints are points of contact between bones or between bones and cartilages, allowing movement. They are classified into fibrous, cartilaginous, and synovial joints.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Joints in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Neuron Structure
text:
Neuron Structure

Key terms: neuron, dendrite, axon

A neuron has three main parts: cell body, dendrites, and axon. Dendrites receive signals, the cell body processes them, and the axon transmits them to other neurons or muscles.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Neuron Structure in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Nerve Impulse Generation
text:
Nerve Impulse Generation

Key terms: nerve impulse, action potential, sodium ions

When stimulated, a neuron's membrane becomes permeable to sodium ions, causing a rapid influx and reversal of the membrane's polarity, generating an action potential or nerve impulse.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Nerve Impulse Generation in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Nerve Impulse Conduction
text:
Nerve Impulse Conduction

Key terms: nerve impulse, axon, depolarization, repolarization

Nerve impulses travel along the axon through a wave of depolarization and repolarization, with the electrical signal moving from one end of the axon to the other.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Nerve Impulse Conduction in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Synapse and Neurotransmitters
text:
Synapse and Neurotransmitters

Key terms: synapse, neurotransmitter, excitatory, inhibitory

A synapse is a junction between neurons where neurotransmitters are released by the presynaptic neuron to influence the postsynaptic neuron, either exciting or inhibiting it.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Synapse and Neurotransmitters in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Central Neural System (CNS)
text:
Central Neural System (CNS)

Key terms: CNS, brain, spinal cord, coordination

The CNS consists of the brain and spinal cord, responsible for information processing, control, and coordination of the body's activities.

metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Central Neural System (CNS) in Grade 11 Biology.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Biology | Forebrain Structure
text:
Forebrain Structure

Key terms: forebrain, cerebrum, thalamus, hypothalamus

A nerve impulse is conducted along the axon membrane as a wave of depolarisation and repolarisation. This process involves the movement of ions, primarily sodium and potassium, across the membrane.

A synapse is formed by the membranes of a pre-synaptic neuron and a post-synaptic neuron, which may or may not be separated by a synaptic cleft. Neurotransmitters are chemicals involved in the transmission of impulses at chemical synapses.

The hindbrain comprises the pons, cerebellum, and medulla. The cerebellum integrates information from the semicircular canals of the ear and the auditory system, while the medulla controls respiration, cardiovascular reflexes, and gastric secretions.
